dataList.content:
Something caught my attention from the corner of my eye after another round of brutal combat.
又一场战斗结束后，我突然注意到脚边有一个闪烁的东西。
dataList.place:
WARP Train Economy Class Cabin
WARP列车 经济舱 车厢

dataList.content:
Huhh...? What's this now?
嗯……？这是什么？

We were on the final car adjacent to the freight car when we discovered that odd box with the T Corp. logo on it.
在与货运车厢相连的最后一节客运车厢里，我们看到了一个带有T公司标志的奇怪的盒子。

Ah, 'tis the emblem of T Corp.!
此乃T公司之标志……！

It appears that the wall covering it was broken in the fierceness of our battle.
似乎已经在战斗中被破坏了。

Didn't that Chief Executive guy... Herbert, right? Didn't he offhandedly mention something about partnering with other Wings?
那个代表……是叫赫伯特吧？我记得他说过和其他翼有很多合作。

I guess they were in cahoots with W Corp. too...
果然和W公司也……

Such collaborations are not limited to T Corp.; it is oft the case that a Wing may work with another.
不仅是T公司，翼之间常常会保持良好关系，进行双向合作。

It is only on rare occasions that they urgently request the assistance of less significant, lesser-known corporations such as our own Limbus Company... Their choice appears to be quite irregular.
倒不如说……我们边狱公司尚且名不见经传，有人如此迫切地向我们寻求合作，的确非同寻常。

Sounds like W Corp.'s heydays are long behind them.
哈，看来W公司也已经彻底衰败了。

Just like this wall that's falling apart, revealing what's behind...
就像这损坏后露出来的墙一样……

... Oh! Speaking of falling apart, this room sure got messed up, huh?
啊！说到损坏……这车厢里本来就乱七八糟的，你们不觉得吗？

It was difficult for me to ignore how Rodya hurriedly swerved to a different subject as though she'd made a mistake. Even the tone of her voice shifted like she was catching herself.
就像是犯了错误一样，罗佳的声音低沉了下来，又恢复了正常。她突然转换话题的样子令我在意。

The various destroyed prosthetic parts covered in human remains indicate that this train car was boarded by several prosthetic-equipped Fixers.
可以看到四处散落着带有血块的义体部件以及碎片，能确认这里就是大多数义体收尾人搭乘的车厢。

... I can't think about that right now. Let's first deal with the task at hand.
……不管怎么说，先从眼前的问题开始解决吧。

Maybe these people are from the same Office as that guy we met at the platform. Remember? He said he'd warped over to T Corp. on an expedition.
之前说去T公司远征的收尾人事务所说不准就是这些人呢。

Look, it's almost like they're all wearing standardized sets of prosthetics. Same make, same model, everything.
有很多相同型号的义体呢……

Mm... I believe I have read articles stating that certain Offices do exclusively hire Fixers with prosthetics.
唔……有些事务所仅会雇用使用义体之收尾人。

Hm...? Wait, he's...
诶……？难道说，他是……

We were walking through the bloodied train car when we suddenly heard Sinclair's voice crack as though he saw something awful.
走在战斗结束后的车厢里的辛克莱仿佛看到了什么不该看到的东西一样，发出了惊恐的声音。

Fie...! He is the one we encountered at the platform...!
啊啊……！其乃吾等于站台上相遇之人……！

This is the Fixer who suddenly started venting at us.
是那个和我们吵架的人。

Yeah, and he said something about going to T Corp. on an expedition and failing... They brought a whole train car full of Fixers for this contract? I guess he wasn't exaggerating when he called it an expedition.
说是来远征，结果失败了吗……有这么多收尾人的话，确实可以称得上货真价实的远征了。

There are over a dozen broken arms strewn about... they must have fought valiantly by replacing their broken arms with backup arms, perchance?
光损坏的手臂总数便已有十数条……乃是通过不断更换预先备好的手臂来战斗的吗？

<Makes sense... That would explain all those broken prosthetic arms and legs in this car.>
<也许正因如此……周围好像散落着很多坏了的义足和义手。>

Executive Manager, This is likely an aftermath of a battle between Fixers and Bloodbags.
我认为那一定是在抵抗其他血袋时留下的痕迹，经理。

There were many similar cases during the war. Those using prosthetics would simply let their bodies be destroyed in battle because they considered them to be disposable as long as their wallets would permit.
在战争时，类似的例子有很多。义体无论何时都可以更换，所以在资金允许的范围内……不必小心保护也能放心战斗。

Of course, the blatant lack of self-preservation often sent them to early graves.
当然，那种家伙往往因为没保护好自己而早早战死。

<Hm, maybe so...>
<是这样吗……>

I see. There are multiple possible interpretations depending on one's perspective, despite the fact that there is but a single scene. I will remember both of your inputs.
看来对于同一种情况，可以有各种各样的理解。我会记住这两种意见的。

Mm, that's a good attitude. Employees with attitude like yours would often make it to the end of the war.
嗯，态度很好。像你这样的员工总能存活到最后。

Yes, well. Good for them.
嗯，是啊。那可真是太好了。

Faust answered Outis in an uncharacteristically snappy manner. Signs of fatigue were creeping into her pensive expression.
一边生硬地回答着，一边忙于某事的浮士德脸上，显露出了明显的疲惫。

<You alright, Faust...?>
<浮士德……你还好吗？>

It was rare to see any actual expression from her... I was starting to get worried.
明明浮士德平常几乎没有表情变化……她还好吗？

I am physically unharmed, but... Hm. Yes, I am alright.
身体上没有问题，不过……嗯，是啊。

However, I do not enjoy this circumstance which we find ourselves in. It is as though I am casting nets to nowhere, lost and isolated in a blind sea.
如同在孤立的海上随意抛网的状况并不令人愉快。

... Normally, deductions such as these would have been completed within moments after establishing a few basic cross-references with the information I accessed.
……平常只要对查阅到的情报进行简单的推理，就能得到明确的结论。

Her voice was such a whisper for the second part of her sentence that even I could barely hear what she was saying.
浮士德的第二句话的声音，轻得连我也只能勉强听清。

Ah, I know what you mean.
啊，我明白你的意思。

Feeling like you're completely lost, obsessively casting net after net over the black, rippleless Lake in desperate hopes that one of them might pull in something we could eat.
在漆黑宁静的湖面上，即便为了获取食物而抛网，不安依然不断积聚。

No way to tell where we are, no way to tell if there's even anything to eat under that glassy water surface... Grasping at the straws, you know?
这里到底是哪里，甚至这里是否能捕获到什么……完全不知道。

This sense I find myself mired in is not unlike your own; it is like lying my back over an unseen grave, for the reflection of radiance upon my eyes and the sanguine scent hanging from the tip of my olfactory sensors tells me naught of the forging path.
我也有如同躺在无形的墓穴中的感觉。仅靠眼前的景象和鼻尖的血腥味，无法判断前进的道路。

It seemed that Ishmael and Yi Sang picked up on the first part of her sentence, however, as they walked up to her and shared a few words of consolation.
大概是听到了前一半的内容，以实玛利和李箱走了过来，说了些安慰浮士德的话。

By the way... I don't ever recall you talking like that, Faust.
但是……这好像是浮士德小姐第一次说这样的话？

I don't know what it is, but I feel like there's... something different about you today?
不，准确来说应该是今天的浮士德小姐感觉与平日不同……

That is...
那是……

Oh, I mean, I don't hate it. I'm actually glad to learn that you had a softer side.
啊，并不是说不好。倒不如说感觉稍微温和一些，还挺好的。

This unseen side of yours... it is unfamiliar, yet quite fresh.
这是我从未见过的样子……十分新鲜。

... Is that so.
……是吗。

Faust's reply was curt. She closed her eyes.
浮士德只是静静地闭上了眼。

As per the information provided by the pamphlet at the platform, it is likely that this train is composed of twelve passenger cars and one freight car.
根据站台上的宣传册，这辆列车由十二节客运车厢和一节货运车厢组成。

Because we are on the eleventh car at the moment, that leaves a single car between us and the freight car in which Mephistopheles is secured.
现在到达的是第十一节车厢。除去梅菲斯托费勒斯所在的第十三节车厢，还剩下一节。

<Which means...>
<那么……>

Which means that there is a high likelihood that we will soon encounter the Bloodfiend responsible for the creation of the Bloodbags aboard this train.
我们很有可能会直面制造这些血袋的血魔。

Just beyond that door...
就在那扇门之后……

Well, how impressive could the leader of this sort of cannon fodder be?
就算这样，顶多就是这群家伙的头目罢了。有什么大的区别呢？

A different, more accurate interpretation would be to say that a being capable of commanding a force as large as the Bloodbags we have defeated should be considered a high-risk entity.
反过来说，正因为它能率领如此多的血袋，将其视为高危的存在比较合理。

Although this is not common knowledge, there is a subcategory of Fixers called Bloodfiend Hunters who specialize in... yes, hunting Bloodfiends.
虽然是鲜为人知的信息，但似乎存在专门处理血魔的收尾人。他们被称为血魔猎人……

Assuming that information is true, it can be inferred that Bloodfiends are difficult foes that require a certain expertise to defeat.
如果信息属实，那么它应该是一个麻烦得需要专家来处理的存在。

Now that I'm thinking about it... if Bloodbags are like mindless thralls to Bloodfiends, then they're kind of like an army, right?
仔细想想的话……这些血袋是盲目地跟随着血魔的某种军队对吧？

A being of power who can create a force of their own without concern for lowered morale or desertion... Wartime or not, they will always make for formidable foes.
能够制造出不用担心士气低下或是逃走的军队的人……无论是战斗还是日常生活中，这样的人都有着非同一般的能力。

The Sinners each exchange various opinions with one another. Possible strategies, estimations of the Bloodfiend's strength...
罪人们互相交换着各种意见，包括对威力的预测，以及应当采取什么战略等。

And all of a sudden...
然后。

Fie on this indecisive idleness!! Our quest is to defeat the villain who hath brought such pain and misery upon this train, is it not?! It may be vaporizing the lifeblood of the innocent as we speak!
勿要再管！！吾等不正是要前往抓捕导致此令人激愤之状况的犯人吗！此时此刻其也可能正在蒸发血液不是吗！

Mighty or feeble, I care not! I swear upon mine honor that I shall smite this foe and let my hand of justice be the judge of their fate! Let us hasten, now!
是否强大，吾不在乎……吾必亲手将其斩杀！动作快些！

Don Quixote's sudden outburst immediately put a stop to the chatter.
在堂吉诃德的怒吼下，罪人们的低语渐渐平息了下来。

<... She's not wrong. Besides, dealing with the Bloodfiend is the key to completing our contract.>
<……是的。而且击败血魔也是解决委托的关键。>

With that, I opened the door leading to the last car of this train.
我和罪人们一起，打开了通往最后一节客运车厢的大门。
